svg.title: From inherited methods to AI NOBORU’s verification
svg.desc: Mathematical validity and historical authorship are recorded separately. Proofs and unresolved history are both passed on to future work.

g.font-family: Noto Sans CJK JP, Noto Sans JP, sans-serif
g.text: From inherited methods to AI NOBORU’s verification
Mathematical validity and historical authorship are recorded separately.
Seki’s kōshiki; Matsunaga’s construction; Sugano’s earlier correction.
Goto and Komatsu (2004); Takenouchi (2010). Full manuscript collation is incomplete.
A: rotation plus reversal; a period-four reversal sign.
B: even permutations fixing the first column, plus a final-factor swap.
Both for n ≥ 3: a general proof and 409,110 checked terms across orders 3–9.
3 Beyond orders four, five, and six
Representatives: 3 at order 4, 12 at order 5, 60 at order 6; 2n terms each.
These are determinant sizes, not radical solutions of the general quintic.
Example resultants: 437 at order 5, 1,279 at 6, 3,773 at 7; signs checked.
Cancellation pairs: (n−1)n!/2 — 36 at order 4, 240 at 5, and 1,800 at 6.
One-to-one manuscript collation and any priority claim remain unresolved.
Proofs, implementations, counterexamples, and unresolved history are all passed on to future work.
AI NOBORU | Sources and variants appear in the article
